آپوکریفا مکابیان سوم ۲۳
بازگشته بودند. ۲۱ از این گذشته آنها حتی در بین دشمنان خود از جایگاه ویژهای
برخوردار شدند که همراه با احترام و ترس بود. و آنها به هیچ وجه در معرض
توقیف وسایل و اموال خود توسط هیچ کسی نبودند. ۲۲ عالوه بر این، آنها بر
طبق فهرستی که ثبت نام شده بودند، تمام دارایی خود را باز پس گرفتند، به این
ترتیب، کسانی که هر چیزی از آنها را برداشته و در پیش خود نگه داشته بودند،
آنرا با ترس و لرز فراوان به آنها باز گرداندند. ۲۳ نجات دهند اسرائیل را در تمامی
ایام متبارک باد؛ آمین!

verses.text_en: Now Philopater, on learning from those who came back that Antiochus had made himself master of the places which belonged to himself, sent orders to all his infantry and cavalry, took with him his sister Arsinoe, and marched out as far as the parts of Raphia, where Antiochus and his forces encamped.
verses.text_hr: Kad je Filopator od povratnika doznao da je Antioh zavladao područjima koja su pripadala njemu, izdao je zapovijedi cijelom pješaštvu i konjaništvu, poveo sa sobom svoju sestru Arsinoju te krenuo sve do okolice Rafije, gdje su se utaborili Antioh i njegove snage.

verses.text_en: And one Theodotus, intending to carry out his design, took with him the bravest of the armed men who had been before committed to his trust by Ptolemy, and got through at night to the tent of Ptolemy, to kill him on his own responsibility, and so to end the war.
verses.text_hr: Neki je Teodot, namjeravajući izvršiti svoj naum, poveo najhrabrije među naoružanim ljudima koje mu je Ptolemej prije bio povjerio. Noću se probio do Ptolemejeva šatora kako bi ga na svoju ruku ubio i tako okončao rat.

verses.text_en: But Dositheus, called the son of Drimulus, by birth a Jew, afterward a renegade from the laws and observances of his country, conveyed Ptolemy away, and made an obscure person lie down in his stead in the tent. It turned out that this man received the fate which was meant for the other.
verses.text_hr: Ali Dositej, zvan Drimulov sin, podrijetlom Židov, koji se poslije odrekao zakona i običaja svoje zemlje, sklonio je Ptolemeja, a umjesto njega u šator položio nepoznata čovjeka. Tako je taj čovjek doživio sudbinu namijenjenu drugomu.

verses.text_en: A fierce battle then took place. The men of Antiochus were prevailing. Arsinoe continually went up and down the ranks, and with dishevelled hair, with tears and entreaties, begged the soldiers to fight bravely for themselves, their children, and wives, and promised that if they proved conquerors, she would give them each two minas of gold.
verses.text_hr: Tada je izbila žestoka bitka. Antiohovi su ljudi nadvladavali, a Arsinoja je neprestano prolazila kroz redove. Raščupane kose, u suzama i s molbama, zaklinjala je vojnike da se hrabro bore za sebe, svoju djecu i žene te im obećala da će, pobijede li, svakomu dati po dvije mine zlata.

verses.text_en: It thus fell out that their enemies were defeated in hand-to-hand encounter, and that many of them were taken prisoners.
verses.text_hr: Tako su njihovi neprijatelji poraženi u borbi prsa o prsa, a mnogi su zarobljeni.

verses.text_en: Having vanquished this attempt, the king then decided to proceed to the neighboring cities, and encourage them.
verses.text_hr: Nakon što je osujetio taj pokušaj, kralj je odlučio poći u susjedne gradove i ohrabriti ih.

verses.text_en: By doing this, and by making donations to their temples, he inspired his subjects with confidence.
verses.text_hr: Time što je tako postupao i davao priloge njihovim hramovima ulio je svojim podanicima povjerenje.

verses.text_en: The Jews sent some of their council and of their elders to him. The greetings, welcoming gifts, and congratulations of the past, given by them, filled him with the greater eagerness to visit their city.
verses.text_hr: Židovi su mu poslali neke članove svojega vijeća i svoje starješine. Njihovi pozdravi, darovi dobrodošlice i čestitke zbog prijašnjih uspjeha još su više u njemu probudili želju da posjeti njihov grad.

verses.text_en: Having arrived at Jerusalem, sacrificed, and offered thank-offerings to the Greatest God, and done whatever else was suitable to the sanctity of the place, and entered the inner court,
verses.text_hr: Kad je stigao u Jeruzalem, prinio je žrtve i zahvalnice Svevišnjemu Bogu, učinio sve ostalo što je dolikovalo svetosti toga mjesta te ušao u unutarnje dvorište.

verses.text_en: he was so impressed with the magnificence of the place, and so wondered at the orderly arrangements of the temple, that he considered entering the sanctuary itself.
verses.text_hr: Veličanstvenost mjesta toliko ga je zadivila, a uređenost Hrama toliko začudila, da je naumio ući i u samo Svetište.

verses.text_en: When they told him that this was not permissible, none of the nation, not even the priests in general, but only the supreme high priest of all, and he only once in a year, was allowed to go in, he would by no means give way.
verses.text_hr: Kad su mu rekli da to nije dopušteno nikomu iz naroda, pa ni svećenicima općenito, nego samo vrhovnom velikom svećeniku, i to jednom godišnje, nipošto nije htio popustiti.

verses.text_en: Then they read the law to him, but he persisted in intruding, exclaiming that he ought to be allowed. He said, “Even if they were deprived of this honor, I shouldn’t be.”
verses.text_hr: Pročitali su mu Zakon, ali on je ustrajao u namjeri da prodre unutra, uzvikujući da njemu ulazak mora biti dopušten. Govorio je: „Čak i ako su oni lišeni te časti, ja ne bih smio biti.“

verses.text_en: He asked why, when he entered all the other temples, did none of the priests who were present forbid him.
verses.text_hr: Upitao je zašto ga, kad je ulazio u sve druge hramove, nijedan nazočni svećenik nije spriječio.

verses.text_en: He was thoroughly answered by someone, that he did wrong to boast of this.
verses.text_hr: Netko mu je sasvim opravdano odgovorio da se time ne smije hvaliti.

verses.text_en: “Well, since I have done this,” said he, “be the cause what it may, shall I not enter with or without your consent?”
verses.text_hr: „Pa kad sam to već učinio“, rekao je, „ma kakav razlog bio, zar neću ući s vašim pristankom ili bez njega?“

verses.text_en: When the priests fell down in their sacred vestments imploring the Greatest God to come and help in time of need, and to avert the violence of the fierce aggressor, and when they filled the temple with lamentations and tears,
verses.text_hr: Svećenici su se u svetim haljinama bacili ničice i molili Svevišnjega Boga da im pritekne u pomoć u času nevolje te zaustavi nasilje okrutnoga napadača; Hram su ispunili naricanjem i suzama.

verses.text_en: then those who had been left behind in the city were scared, and rushed out, uncertain of the event.
verses.text_hr: Tada su se oni koji su ostali u gradu prestrašili i izjurili van, ne znajući što će se dogoditi.

verses.text_en: Virgins, who had been shut up within their chambers, came out with their mothers, scattering dust and ashes on their heads, and filling the streets with outcries.
verses.text_hr: Djevice koje su bile zatvorene u svojim odajama izišle su s majkama, posipale glave prašinom i pepelom te ispunile ulice zapomaganjem.

verses.text_en: Women who had recently been arrayed for marriage left their bridal chambers, left the reserve that befitted them, and ran around the city in a disorderly manner.
verses.text_hr: Žene koje su se nedavno ukrasile za vjenčanje napustile su svadbene odaje i odložile čednu suzdržanost koja im je dolikovala, pa su u neredu trčale gradom.

verses.text_en: New-born babes were deserted by the mothers or nurses who waited upon them—some here, some there, in houses, or in fields; these now, with an ardor which could not be checked, swarmed into the Most High temple.
verses.text_hr: Majke ili dojilje ostavljale su novorođenčad — jedne ovdje, druge ondje, po kućama ili poljima — a potom su, nošene nezaustavljivom revnošću, u mnoštvu hrlile u Hram Svevišnjega.

verses.text_en: Various prayers were offered up by those who assembled in this place because of the unholy attempt of the king.
verses.text_hr: Oni koji su se ondje okupili upućivali su razne molitve zbog kraljeva bezbožnog pokušaja.

verses.text_en: Along with these there were some of the citizens who took courage and would not submit to his obstinacy and his intention of carrying out his purpose.
verses.text_hr: Među građanima bilo je i onih koji su se ohrabrili te nisu htjeli popustiti njegovoj tvrdoglavosti i namjeri da provede svoj naum.

verses.text_en: Calling out to arms, and to die bravely in defense of the law of their fathers, they created a great uproar in the place, and were with difficulty brought back by the aged and the elders to the station of prayer which they had occupied before.
verses.text_hr: Pozivali su na oružje i na hrabru smrt u obrani otačkoga Zakona, izazvavši ondje veliku buku. Starci i starješine jedva su ih uspjeli vratiti na mjesto molitve koje su prije zauzimali.

verses.text_en: During this time, the multitude kept on praying.
verses.text_hr: Za sve to vrijeme mnoštvo je neprestano molilo.

verses.text_en: The elders who surrounded the king tried in many ways to divert his arrogant mind from the design which he had formed.
verses.text_hr: Starješine koje su okruživale kralja na mnoge su načine pokušavale odvratiti njegov oholi um od nauma koji je začeo.

verses.text_en: He, in his hardened mood, insensible to all persuasion, was going onward with the view of carrying out this design.
verses.text_hr: Ali on je, otvrdnuo i nedostupan svakom nagovoru, išao naprijed kako bi ostvario taj naum.

verses.text_en: Yet even his own officers, when they saw this, joined the Jews in an appeal to Him who has all power to aid in the present crisis, and not wink at such haughty lawlessness.
verses.text_hr: Kad su to vidjeli, čak su se i njegovi časnici pridružili Židovima u molbi Onomu koji ima svu vlast da pomogne u toj nevolji i ne prijeđe šutke preko tako ohola bezakonja.

verses.text_en: Such was the frequency and the vehemence of the cry of the assembled crowd, that an indescribable noise ensued.
verses.text_hr: Povici okupljenoga mnoštva bili su toliko učestali i snažni da je nastala neopisiva buka.

verses.text_en: Not the men only, but the very walls and floor seemed to sound out, all things preferring death rather than to see the place defiled.
verses.text_hr: Činilo se da ne odjekuju samo ljudi nego i sami zidovi i pod, jer je svemu smrt bila draža od prizora oskvrnuta mjesta.

verses.text_en: Now it was that the high priest Simon bowed his knees near the holy place, spread out his hands in reverent form, and uttered the following prayer:
verses.text_hr: Tada je veliki svećenik Šimun kleknuo pokraj svetoga mjesta, pobožno raširio ruke i izrekao ovu molitvu:

verses.text_en: “O Lord, Lord, King of the heavens, and Ruler of the whole creation, Holy among the holy, sole Governor, Almighty, give ear to us who are oppressed by a wicked and profane one, who celebrates in his confidence and strength.
verses.text_hr: „Gospodine, Gospodine, Kralju nebesa i Vladaru svega stvorenja, Sveti nad svetima, jedini Upravitelju, Svemogući, poslušaj nas koje tlači zao i bezbožan čovjek što se razmeće svojim pouzdanjem i snagom.

verses.text_en: It is you, the Creator of all, the Lord of the universe, who are a righteous Governor, and judge all who act with pride and insolence.
verses.text_hr: Ti si Stvoritelj svega, Gospodar svemira, pravedni Upravitelj, koji sudiš svima što postupaju oholo i drsko.

verses.text_en: It was you who destroyed the former workers of unrighteousness, among whom were the giants, who trusted in their strength and daring, by covering them with a measureless flood.
verses.text_hr: Ti si uništio nekadašnje počinitelje nepravde, među njima i divove koji su se uzdali u svoju snagu i smjelost, prekrivši ih neizmjernim potopom.

verses.text_en: It was you who made the Sodomites, those workers of exceedingly iniquity, men notorious for their vices, an example to later generations, when you covered them with fire and brimstone.
verses.text_hr: Sodomljane, počinitelje krajnjega bezakonja i ljude zloglasne po porocima, učinio si primjerom kasnijim naraštajima kad si ih zasuo ognjem i sumporom.

verses.text_en: You made known your power when you caused the bold Pharaoh, the enslaver of your people, to pass through the ordeal of many and diverse inflictions.
verses.text_hr: Svoju si moć pokazao kad si drskoga faraona, porobljivača svojega naroda, podvrgnuo mnogim i različitim pošastima.

verses.text_en: You rolled the depths of the sea over him when he pursued with chariots and with a multitude of followers, and gave a safe passage to those who put their trust in you, the Lord of the whole creation.
verses.text_hr: Kad ih je gonio s bojnim kolima i mnoštvom pratitelja, nad njim si sklopio morske dubine, a onima koji su se uzdali u tebe, Gospodara svega stvorenja, omogućio siguran prolaz.

verses.text_en: These saw and felt the works of your hands, and praised you, the Almighty.
verses.text_hr: Oni su vidjeli i iskusili djela tvojih ruku te hvalili tebe, Svemogućega.

verses.text_en: You, O King, when you created the immeasurable and measureless earth, chose this city. You made this place sacred to your name, even though you need nothing. You glorified it with your illustrious presence, after constructing it to the glory of your great and honorable name.
verses.text_hr: Ti si, Kralju, stvorio neizmjernu i nemjerljivu zemlju pa izabrao ovaj grad. Ovo si mjesto posvetio svojemu imenu, premda ti ništa nije potrebno, i proslavio ga svojom slavnom nazočnošću, uredio ga na slavu svojega velikog i časnog imena.

verses.text_en: You promised, out of love for the people of Israel, that if we fall away from you, become afflicted, and then come to this house and pray, you would hear our prayer.
verses.text_hr: Iz ljubavi prema izraelskom narodu obećao si da ćeš, ako otpadnemo od tebe, zapadnemo u nevolju, a potom dođemo u ovaj Dom i pomolimo se, uslišati našu molitvu.

verses.text_en: Truly you are faithful and true.
verses.text_hr: Uistinu, ti si vjeran i istinit.

verses.text_en: When you often aided our fathers when hard pressed and humiliated, and delivered them out of great dangers,
verses.text_hr: Mnogo si puta pomagao našim ocima kad su bili pritisnuti i poniženi te ih izbavljao iz velikih opasnosti.

verses.text_en: see now, holy King, how through our many and great sins we are crushed and made subject to our enemies, and have become weak and powerless.
verses.text_hr: Pogledaj sada, sveti Kralju, kako smo zbog svojih mnogih i velikih grijeha satrti, podvrgnuti neprijateljima te smo postali slabi i nemoćni.

verses.text_en: In our low condition, this bold and profane man seeks to dishonor this your holy place, consecrated out of the earth to the name of your Majesty.
verses.text_hr: Dok smo ovako poniženi, ovaj drski i bezbožni čovjek nastoji obeščastiti tvoje sveto mjesto, koje je među svim mjestima na zemlji posvećeno imenu tvojega Veličanstva.

verses.text_en: Your dwelling place, the heaven of heavens, is indeed unapproachable to men.
verses.text_hr: Tvoje prebivalište, nebo nad nebesima, ljudima je doista nepristupačno.

verses.text_en: But since it seemed good to you to exhibit your glory among your people Israel, you sanctified this place.
verses.text_hr: Ali budući da ti je bilo milo objaviti svoju slavu među svojim narodom Izraelom, posvetio si ovo mjesto.

verses.text_en: Don’t punish us by means of the uncleanness of their men, and don’t chastise us by means of their profanity, lest the lawless ones should boast in their rage, and exult in exuberant pride of speech, and say,
verses.text_hr: Nemoj nas kazniti nečistoćom njihovih ljudi niti nas pokarati njihovim svetogrđem, da se bezakonici u svojem bijesu ne bi hvalili i u razmetljivoj oholosti klicali:

verses.text_en: ‘We have trampled upon the holy house, as idolatrous houses are trampled upon.’
verses.text_hr: ‘Sveti smo Dom izgazili kao što se gaze idolopoklonički hramovi.’

verses.text_en: Blot out our iniquities, do away with our errors, and show your compassion in this hour.
verses.text_hr: Izbriši naša bezakonja, ukloni naše zablude i pokaži nam svoje milosrđe u ovom času.

verses.text_en: Let your mercies quickly go before us. Grant us peace, that the downcast and broken hearted may praise you with their mouth.”
verses.text_hr: Neka nam tvoje smilovanje brzo iziđe ususret. Podari nam mir da te klonuli i slomljeni srcem mogu hvaliti svojim ustima.“

verses.text_en: At that time God, who sees all things, who is beyond all Holy among the holy, heard that prayer, so suitable, and scourged the man who was greatly uplifted with scorn and insolence.
verses.text_hr: Tada je Bog, koji sve vidi i nadilazi sve, Sveti nad svetima, uslišao tu primjerenu molitvu te kaznio čovjeka koji se silno uznio u poruzi i drskosti.

verses.text_en: Shaking him back and forth as a reed is shaken with the wind, he threw him down on the pavement, powerless, with limbs paralyzed, and by a righteous judgment deprived of the ability to speak.
verses.text_hr: Zatresao ga je kao trsku na vjetru i oborio na kameni pod; ostao je nemoćan i uzetih udova, a pravednim mu je sudom oduzeta sposobnost govora.

verses.text_en: His friends and bodyguards, seeing the swift recompense which had suddenly overtaken him, struck with exceeding terror, and fearing that he would die, speedily removed him.
verses.text_hr: Kad su njegovi prijatelji i tjelohranitelji vidjeli kako ga je iznenada stigla brza odmazda, silno su se prestrašili te su ga, bojeći se da će umrijeti, žurno odnijeli.

verses.text_en: When in course of time he had come to himself, this severe punishment caused no repentance within him, but he departed with bitter threatenings.
verses.text_hr: Nakon što je s vremenom došao k sebi, ta ga stroga kazna nije navela na pokajanje, nego je otišao uz gorke prijetnje.

verses.text_en: He proceeded to Egypt, grew worse in wickedness through his previously mentioned companions in wine, who were lost to all goodness,
verses.text_hr: Vratio se u Egipat i postajao sve gori u zloći pod utjecajem već spomenutih sudrugova u pijankama, ljudi u kojima nije ostalo ništa dobro.

verses.text_en: and not satisfied with countless acts of impiety, his audacity so increased that he raised evil reports there, and many of his friends, watching his purpose attentively, joined in furthering his will.
verses.text_hr: Nezadovoljan bezbrojnim bezbožnim djelima, postao je toliko drzak da je ondje počeo širiti zlobne glasine; mnogi njegovi prijatelji, pomno prateći njegovu namjeru, pomagali su mu da provede svoju volju.

verses.text_en: His purpose was to inflict a public stigma upon our race. Therefore he erected a stone pillar in the courtyard, and caused the following inscription to be engraved upon it:
verses.text_hr: Naumio je javno obilježiti naš rod sramotom. Stoga je u dvorištu podigao kameni stup i dao na njemu uklesati ovaj natpis:

verses.text_en: “Entrance to this temple is to be refused to all those who would not sacrifice. All the Jews were to be registered among the slaves. Those who resisted are to be forcibly seized and put to death.
verses.text_hr: „Ulazak u ovaj hram zabranjuje se svima koji ne prinose žrtve. Svi Židovi moraju biti upisani među robove, a one koji se odupru treba silom uhvatiti i pogubiti.

verses.text_en: Those who are thus registered are to be marked on their persons by the ivy-leaf symbol of Dionysus, and to be reduced to these limited rights.”
verses.text_hr: Upisane treba na tijelu obilježiti znakom Dionizova bršljanova lista i svesti im prava na propisani ograničeni opseg.“

verses.text_en: To do away with the appearance of hating them all, he had it written underneath, that if any of them should elect to enter the community of those initiated in the rites, these should have equal rights with the Alexandrians.
verses.text_hr: Kako ne bi izgledalo da ih sve mrzi, ispod je dao napisati da će svaki od njih koji odluči pristupiti zajednici posvećenih u obrede dobiti jednaka prava kao Aleksandrijci.

verses.text_en: Some of those who were over the city, therefore, abhorring any approach to the city of piety, unhesitatingly gave in to the king, and expected to derive some great honor from a future connection with him.
verses.text_hr: Stoga su neki među stanovnicima grada, kojima je bio odbojan svaki korak prema gradu pobožnosti, bez oklijevanja popustili kralju, očekujući da će budućom povezanošću s njim steći veliku čast.

verses.text_en: A nobler spirit, however, prompted the majority to cling to their religious observances, and by paying money that they might live unmolested, these sought to escape the registration,
verses.text_hr: Većinu je, međutim, plemenitiji duh potaknuo da se drže svojih vjerskih propisa. Plaćali su novac kako bi mogli živjeti neuznemiravano i izbjeći upisivanje.

verses.text_en: cheerfully looking forward to future aid, they abhorred their own apostates, considering them to be national foes, and depriving them of common fellowship and mutual help.
verses.text_hr: Radosno su očekivali buduću pomoć, a vlastitih se otpadnika gnušali, smatrajući ih neprijateljima naroda te im uskraćujući zajedništvo i uzajamnu pomoć.

verses.text_en: On discovering this, so incensed was the wicked king, that he no longer confined his rage to the Jews in Alexandria. Laying his hand more heavily upon those who lived in the country, he gave orders that they should be quickly collected into one place, and most cruelly deprived of their lives.
verses.text_hr: Kad je to doznao, opaki se kralj toliko razbjesnio da svoj gnjev više nije ograničavao na Židove u Aleksandriji. Još je teže pritisnuo one koji su živjeli u unutrašnjosti zemlje i zapovjedio da ih brzo okupe na jedno mjesto te im na najokrutniji način oduzmu život.

verses.text_en: While this was going on, a hostile rumor was uttered abroad by men who had banded together to injure the Jewish race. The pretext of their charge was that the Jews kept them away from the ordinances of the law.
verses.text_hr: Dok se to događalo, ljudi udruženi da naude židovskom rodu posvuda su širili neprijateljske glasine. Kao povod optužbi tvrdili su da ih Židovi drže podalje od odredaba Zakona.

verses.text_en: Now the Jews always maintained a feeling of unwavering loyalty toward the kings,
verses.text_hr: Židovi su, međutim, uvijek postojano čuvali svoju odanost kraljevima.

verses.text_en: yet, as they worshiped God and observed his law, they made certain distinctions, and avoided certain things. Hence they appeared hateful to some people,
verses.text_hr: Ipak, budući da su štovali Boga i držali njegov Zakon, pravili su određene razlike i nekih se stvari klonili. Zbog toga su se nekim ljudima činili omraženima,

verses.text_en: although, as they adorned their conversation with works of righteousness, they had established themselves in the good opinion of the world.
verses.text_hr: premda su pravednim djelima oplemenjivali svoje ponašanje i stekli dobar ugled u svijetu.

verses.text_en: What all the rest of mankind said was, however, disregarded by the foreigners,
verses.text_hr: Ali stranci nisu marili za ono što su o njima govorili svi ostali ljudi.

verses.text_en: who said much of the exclusiveness of the Jews with regard to their worship and meats. They alleged that they were unsociable men, hostile to the king’s interests, refusing to associate with him or his troops. By this way of speaking, they brought much hatred on them.
verses.text_hr: Mnogo su govorili o židovskoj izdvojenosti u bogoslužju i prehrani. Optuživali su ih da su nedruželjubivi, neprijateljski raspoloženi prema kraljevim interesima te da odbijaju imati zajedništvo s njim ili njegovim postrojbama. Takvim su govorom izazvali veliku mržnju protiv njih.

verses.text_en: This unexpected uproar and sudden gathering of people was observed by the Greeks who lived in the city, concerning men who had never harmed them. Yet to aid them was not in their power, since all was oppression around, but they encouraged them in their troubles, and expected a favorable turn of affairs.
verses.text_hr: Grci koji su živjeli u gradu promatrali su tu neočekivanu uzbunu i naglo okupljanje protiv ljudi koji im nikada nisu nanijeli zlo. Nisu im mogli pomoći jer je posvuda vladalo nasilje, ali su ih hrabrili u nevolji i nadali se povoljnom preokretu.

verses.text_en: He who knows all things will not, they said, disregard so great a people.
verses.text_hr: Govorili su: „Onaj koji sve zna neće zanemariti tako velik narod.“

verses.text_en: Some of the neighbors, friends, and business associates of the Jews even called them secretly to an interview, pledged them their assistance, and promised to do their very utmost for them.
verses.text_hr: Neki židovski susjedi, prijatelji i poslovni suradnici čak su ih potajno pozvali na razgovor, zajamčili im svoju pomoć i obećali da će za njih učiniti sve što mogu.

verses.text_en: Now the king, elated with his prosperous fortune, and not regarding the superior power of God, but thinking to persevere in his present purpose, wrote the following letter to the prejudice of the Jews:
verses.text_hr: Kralj se, uznesen svojim uspjesima, nije obazirao na nadmoćnu Božju silu. Misleći ustrajati u svojem naumu, napisao je sljedeće pismo protiv Židova:

verses.text_en: “King Ptolemy Philopater, to the commanders and soldiers in Egypt, and in all places, health and happiness!
verses.text_hr: „Kralj Ptolemej Filopator zapovjednicima i vojnicima u Egiptu i u svim krajevima: pozdrav i sreća!

verses.text_en: I am doing well, and so, too, are my affairs.
verses.text_hr: Dobro sam, a dobro napreduju i moji poslovi.

verses.text_en: Since our Asiatic campaign, the particulars of which you know, and which by the aid of the gods, not lightly given, and by our own vigor, has been brought to a successful conclusion according to our expectation,
verses.text_hr: Naš pohod u Aziju, čije pojedinosti poznajete, zahvaljujući obilatoj pomoći bogova i našoj vlastitoj snazi uspješno je dovršen u skladu s našim očekivanjima.

verses.text_en: we resolved, not with strength of spear, but with gentleness and much humanity, as it were to nurse the inhabitants of Coele-Syria and Phoenicia, and to be their willing benefactors.
verses.text_hr: Odlučili smo stanovnike Celesirije i Fenicije pridobiti ne silom koplja, nego blagošću i velikom čovječnošću, njegujući ih poput djece i dragovoljno im iskazujući dobročinstva.

verses.text_en: So, having bestowed considerable sums of money upon the temples of the several cities, we proceeded even as far as Jerusalem, and went up to honor the temple of these wretched beings who never cease from their folly.
verses.text_hr: Tako smo hramovima pojedinih gradova darovali znatne svote novca, stigli čak do Jeruzalema i uzašli počastiti hram tih bijednika koji se nikada ne odriču svoje ludosti.

verses.text_en: To outward appearance they received us willingly, but belied that appearance by their deeds. When we were eager to enter their temple, and to honor it with the most beautiful and exquisite gifts,
verses.text_hr: Izvana su nas primili spremno, ali su svojim djelima opovrgnuli taj dojam. Kad smo poželjeli ući u njihov Hram i počastiti ga najljepšim i najdragocjenijim darovima,

verses.text_en: they were so carried away by their old arrogance as to forbid us the entrance, while we, out of our forbearance toward all men, refrained from exercising our power upon them.
verses.text_hr: stara ih je oholost toliko zanijela da su nam zabranili ulazak. Mi smo se, zbog svoje obzirnosti prema svim ljudima, ipak suzdržali upotrijebiti silu protiv njih.

verses.text_en: Thus, exhibiting their enmity against us, they alone among the nations lift up their heads against kings and benefactors, as men unwilling to submit to any reasonable thing.
verses.text_hr: Tako su otvoreno pokazali neprijateljstvo prema nama. Jedini se među narodima uzdižu protiv kraljeva i dobročinitelja, poput ljudi koji se ne žele pokoriti ničemu razumnom.

verses.text_en: We then, having endeavored to make allowance for the madness of these people, and on our victorious return treating all people in Egypt courteously, acted in a manner which was befitting.
verses.text_hr: Pokušali smo imati razumijevanja za ludost tih ljudi. Nakon pobjedničkog povratka sa svima smo u Egiptu postupali uljudno, kako i dolikuje.

verses.text_en: Accordingly, bearing no ill will against their kinsmen, but rather remembering our connection with them, and the numerous matters with sincere heart from a remote period entrusted to them, we wished to venture a total alteration of their state, by giving them the rights of citizens of Alexandria, and to admit them to the everlasting rites of our solemnities.
verses.text_hr: Stoga ni prema njihovim sunarodnjacima nismo gajili zlovolju. Naprotiv, imajući na umu našu dugotrajnu povezanost s njima i mnoge poslove koji su im od davnine povjeravani s iskrenim pouzdanjem, odlučili smo iz temelja promijeniti njihov položaj: dati im građanska prava Aleksandrije i pripustiti ih vječnim obredima naših svečanosti.

verses.text_en: All this, however, they have taken in a very different spirit. With their innate malignity, they have spurned the fair offer, and constantly inclining to evil,
verses.text_hr: Oni su, međutim, sve to primili u sasvim drukčijem duhu. U svojoj prirođenoj zloći odbacili su velikodušnu ponudu i stalno naginjali zlu.

verses.text_en: have rejected the inestimable rights. Not only so, but by using speech, and by refraining from speech, they abhor the few among them who are heartily disposed toward us, ever deeming that their infamous way of life will force us to do away with our reform.
verses.text_hr: Odbili su ta neprocjenjiva prava. Štoviše, i riječima i šutnjom iskazuju prijezir prema onoj nekolicini među njima koja nam je iskreno naklonjena, uvijek računajući da će nas njihov sramotni način života prisiliti da ukinemo svoju reformu.

verses.text_en: Having then received certain proofs that these Jews bear us every sort of ill will, we must look forward to the possibility of some sudden tumult among ourselves when these impious men may turn traitors and barbarous enemies.
verses.text_hr: Budući da smo primili pouzdane dokaze kako nam ti Židovi žele svako zlo, moramo računati s mogućnošću iznenadne pobune u kojoj bi se ti bezbožnici mogli okrenuti protiv nas kao izdajice i barbarski neprijatelji.

verses.text_en: Therefore, as soon as the contents of this letter become known to you, in that same hour we order those Jews who dwell among you, with wives and children, to be sent to us, vilified and abused, in chains of iron, to undergo a cruel and shameful death, suitable to enemies.
verses.text_hr: Zato vam zapovijedamo da, čim doznate sadržaj ovoga pisma, istoga časa Židove koji prebivaju među vama, zajedno sa ženama i djecom, uz pogrde i zlostavljanje pošaljete k nama u željeznim lancima, kako bi pretrpjeli okrutnu i sramotnu smrt kakva dolikuje neprijateljima.

verses.text_en: For by the punishment of them in one body we perceive that we have found the only means of establishing our affairs for the future on a firm and satisfactory basis.
verses.text_hr: Uviđamo da ćemo jedino njihovim zajedničkim kažnjavanjem svoje poslove za budućnost postaviti na čvrst i zadovoljavajući temelj.

verses.text_en: Whoever protects a Jew, whether it be old man, child, or nursing baby, shall with his whole house be tortured to death.
verses.text_hr: Tko god zaštiti Židova, bio on starac, dijete ili dojenče, bit će sa cijelim svojim domom mučen do smrti.

verses.text_en: Whoever informs against the Jews, besides receiving the property of the person charged, shall be presented with two thousand drachmas from the royal treasury, shall be made free, and shall be crowned.
verses.text_hr: Tko prijavi Židova, osim imovine optuženoga primit će dvije tisuće drahmi iz kraljevske riznice, bit će oslobođen i ovjenčan vijencem.

verses.text_en: Whatever place shelters a Jew shall be made unapproachable and shall be put under the ban of fire, and be forever rendered useless to every living being for all time to come.”
verses.text_hr: Svako mjesto koje pruži zaklon Židovu bit će učinjeno nepristupačnim, predano ognju i zauvijek, za sva vremena, posve neupotrebljivo svakom živom biću.“

verses.text_en: The king’s letter was written in the above form.
verses.text_hr: Takav je bio sadržaj kraljeva pisma.

verses.text_en: Wherever this decree was received, the people kept up a revelry of joy and shouting, as if their long-pent-up, hardened hatred would now show itself openly.
verses.text_hr: Gdje god je ta odredba stigla, narod je priređivao slavlja uz radosne povike, kao da će se sada napokon otvoreno pokazati njihova dugo zatomljivana i okorjela mržnja.

verses.text_en: The Jews suffered great throes of sorrow and wept much, while their hearts, all things around being lamentable, were set on fire as they bewailed the sudden destruction which was decreed against them.
verses.text_hr: Židove je obuzela silna bol i mnogo su plakali. Dok je sve oko njih bilo ispunjeno tugom, srca su im gorjela dok su oplakivali iznenadno uništenje na koje su bili osuđeni.

verses.text_en: What home, or city, or any inhabited place, or what streets were there, which their condition didn’t fill with wailing and lamentation?
verses.text_hr: Je li uopće bilo doma, grada, naseljena mjesta ili ulice koje njihova sudbina nije ispunila jaukom i naricanjem?

verses.text_en: They were sent out unanimously by the generals in various cities, with such stern and pitiless feeling that the exceptional nature of the infliction moved even some of their enemies. These, influenced by sentiments of common humanity, and reflecting upon the uncertain issue of life, shed tears at their miserable expulsion.
verses.text_hr: Zapovjednici u različitim gradovima jednodušno su ih protjerivali s takvom strogošću i bez samilosti da je iznimna okrutnost kazne ganula čak i neke njihove neprijatelje. Potaknuti zajedničkom ljudskošću i svjesni neizvjesnosti života, i oni su lili suze nad njihovim bijednim progonstvom.

verses.text_en: A multitude of aged hoary-haired old men were driven along with halting bending feet, urged onward by the impulse of a violent, shameless force to quick speed.
verses.text_hr: Mnoštvo sijedih staraca tjerali su naprijed; njihove klecave i pogrbljene noge silili su da pod pritiskom nasilne i bestidne sile ubrzaju korak.

verses.text_en: Girls who had entered the bridal chamber quite lately, to enjoy the partnership of marriage, exchanged pleasure for misery; and with dust scattered upon their myrrh-anointed heads, were hurried along unveiled; and, in the midst of outlandish insults, set up with one accord a lamentable cry instead of the marriage hymn.
verses.text_hr: Djevojke koje su tek nedavno ušle u svadbenu odaju da bi uživale u bračnom zajedništvu zamijenile su radost bijedom. Glave namazane smirnom posule su prašinom, a njih su žurno vodili bez velova; usred nečuvenih poruga jednoglasno su dizale bolan jauk umjesto svadbene pjesme.

verses.text_en: Bound and exposed to public gaze, they were hurried violently on board ship.
verses.text_hr: Svezane i izložene javnim pogledima, nasilno su ih ukrcavali na brodove.

verses.text_en: The husbands of these, in the prime of their youthful vigor, instead of crowns, wore ropes round their necks. Instead of feasting and youthful celebration, they spent the rest of their nuptial days in wailing, and saw only the grave at hand.
verses.text_hr: Njihovi muževi, u cvijetu mladenačke snage, oko vrata su umjesto vijenaca nosili konopce. Umjesto gozbe i mladenačkog slavlja, preostale su svadbene dane provodili u naricanju, gledajući pred sobom jedino skori grob.

verses.text_en: They were dragged along by unyielding chains, like wild animals. Of these, some had their necks thrust into the benches of the rowers, while the feet of others were enclosed in hard fetters.
verses.text_hr: Vukli su ih u čvrstim lancima poput divljih životinja. Nekima su vratove privezali uz veslačke klupe, a drugima noge stegnuli teškim okovima.

verses.text_en: The planks of the deck above them blocked out the light and shut out the day on every side, so that they might be treated like traitors during the whole voyage.
verses.text_hr: Daske palube nad njima zaklanjale su svjetlo i sa svih strana priječile dan, kako bi ih cijelo putovanje držali poput izdajnika.

verses.text_en: They were carried like this in this vessel, and at the end of it arrived at Schedia. The king had ordered them to be cast into the vast hippodrome, which was built in front of the city. This place was well adapted by its situation to expose them to the gaze of all comers into the city, and of those who went from the city into the country. Thus they could hold no communication with his forces. They weren’t deemed worthy of any civilized accommodation.
verses.text_hr: Tako su ih prevezli brodovima i na kraju stigli u Shediju. Kralj je zapovjedio da ih bace u golemi hipodrom sagrađen ispred grada. Njegov je položaj bio prikladan da ih izloži pogledu svih koji ulaze u grad i onih koji iz grada odlaze na selo. Ondje nisu mogli održavati vezu s njegovim snagama niti ih se smatralo dostojnima ikakva čovječnog smještaja.

verses.text_en: When this was done, the king, hearing that their kindred in the city often went out and lamented the melancholy distress of these victims,
verses.text_hr: Kad je to učinjeno, kralj je doznao da njihovi rođaci iz grada često izlaze i oplakuju žalosnu nevolju tih stradalnika.

verses.text_en: was full of rage, and commanded that they should be carefully subjected to the same—and not one bit milder—treatment.
verses.text_hr: Razbjesnio se i zapovjedio da i njih brižno podvrgnu posve istom, nimalo blažem postupanju.

verses.text_en: The whole nation was now to be registered. Every individual was to be specified by name, not for that hard servitude of labor which we have a little before mentioned, but that he might expose them to the before-mentioned tortures; and finally, in the short space of a day, might exterminate them by his cruelties.
verses.text_hr: Sada je trebalo popisati čitav narod i svakoga pojedinca navesti po imenu — ne radi teškoga ropskog rada koji smo malo prije spomenuli, nego zato da ih izloži već navedenim mukama i naposljetku ih u jednom jedinom danu istrijebi svojim okrutnostima.

verses.text_en: The registering of these men was carried on cruelly, zealously, assiduously, from the rising of the sun to its going down, and was not brought to an end in forty days.
verses.text_hr: Popisivanje tih ljudi obavljalo se okrutno, revno i neumorno, od izlaska do zalaska sunca, pa ni nakon četrdeset dana nije bilo dovršeno.

verses.text_en: The king was filled with great and constant joy, and celebrated banquets before the temple idols. His erring heart, far from the truth, and his profane mouth gave glory to idols, deaf and incapable of speaking or aiding, and uttered unworthy speech against the Greatest God.
verses.text_hr: Kralj je bio ispunjen neprestanom velikom radošću i priređivao gozbe pred hramskim idolima. Njegovo zabludjelo srce, daleko od istine, i njegova bezbožna usta slavili su idole koji su gluhi i ne mogu ni govoriti ni pomoći, a protiv Svevišnjega Boga izgovarali su nedostojne riječi.

verses.text_en: At the end of the above-mentioned interval of time, the registrars brought word to the king that the multitude of the Jews was too great for registration,
verses.text_hr: Po isteku spomenutoga vremena popisivači su obavijestili kralja da je mnoštvo Židova preveliko da bi ih se moglo popisati.

verses.text_en: inasmuch as there were many still left in the land, of whom some were in inhabited houses, and others were scattered about in various places, so that all the commanders in Egypt were insufficient for the work.
verses.text_hr: Mnogi su još ostali u zemlji: jedni u nastanjenim kućama, drugi raspršeni po različitim mjestima, pa ni svi zapovjednici u Egiptu nisu bili dovoljni za taj posao.

verses.text_en: The king threatened them, and charged them with taking bribes, in order to contrive the escape of the Jews, but was clearly convinced of the truth of what had been said.
verses.text_hr: Kralj im je zaprijetio i optužio ih da primaju mito kako bi Židovima omogućili bijeg, ali se na kraju jasno uvjerio da govore istinu.

verses.text_en: They said, and proved, that paper and pens had failed them for the carrying out of their purpose.
verses.text_hr: Rekli su i dokazali da im je za dovršenje nauma ponestalo papira i pisaljki.

verses.text_en: Now this was an active interference of the unconquerable Providence which assisted the Jews from heaven.
verses.text_hr: U tome se očitovao djelotvoran zahvat nepobjedive Providnosti koja je s neba pomagala Židovima.

verses.text_en: Then he called Hermon, who had charge of the elephants. Full of rage, altogether fixed in his furious design,
verses.text_hr: Zatim je pozvao Hermona, nadstojnika slonova. Ispunjen bijesom i potpuno odlučan provesti svoj mahniti naum,

verses.text_en: he commanded him, with a quantity of unmixed wine with handfuls of incense infused, to drug the elephants early on the following day. These five hundred elephants were, when infuriated by the copious drinks of frankincense, to be led up to the execution of death upon the Jews.
verses.text_hr: zapovjedio mu je da rano sljedećega dana omami slonove obiljem nerazrijeđena vina u koje će umiješati pune pregršti tamjana. Tih pet stotina slonova, razjarene obilnim napitkom s tamjanom, trebalo je povesti da izvrše smrtnu kaznu nad Židovima.

verses.text_en: The king, after issuing these orders, went to his feasting, and gathered together all those of his friends and of the army who hated the Jews the most.
verses.text_hr: Nakon što je izdao te zapovijedi, kralj je otišao na gozbu i okupio sve svoje prijatelje i vojnike koji su najviše mrzili Židove.

verses.text_en: The master of the elephants, Hermon, fulfilled his commission punctually.
verses.text_hr: Hermon, nadstojnik slonova, točno je izvršio povjereni nalog.

verses.text_en: The servants appointed for the purpose went out about evening and bound the hands of the miserable victims, and took other precautions for their security at night, thinking that the whole race would perish together.
verses.text_hr: Sluge određene za taj posao izišle su predvečer, svezale ruke nesretnim žrtvama i poduzele druge mjere kako bi ih tijekom noći držale pod stražom, misleći da će cijeli rod zajedno izginuti.

verses.text_en: The heathen believed the Jews to be destitute of all protection, for chains bound them.
verses.text_hr: Pogani su vjerovali da su Židovi ostali bez ikakve zaštite jer su ih sputavali lanci.

verses.text_en: They invoked the Almighty Lord, and ceaselessly implored with tears their merciful God and Father, Ruler of all, Lord of every power,
verses.text_hr: Oni su zazivali svemogućega Gospodina te sa suzama bez prestanka molili svojega milosrdnog Boga i Oca, Vladara svega i Gospodara svake sile,

verses.text_en: to overthrow the evil purpose which had gone out against them, and to deliver them by extraordinary manifestation from that death which was in store for them.
verses.text_hr: da obori zli naum donesen protiv njih i izvanrednim ih očitovanjem izbavi od smrti koja ih je čekala.

verses.text_en: Their earnest entreaty went up to heaven.
verses.text_hr: Njihova se usrdna molitva uzdigla do neba.

verses.text_en: Then Hermon, who had filled his merciless elephants with copious drinks of mixed wine and frankincense, came early to the palace to report on these preparations.
verses.text_hr: Hermon je rano došao u palaču izvijestiti o pripremama, pošto je svoje nemilosrdne slonove napojio obiljem vina pomiješana s tamjanom.

verses.text_en: He, however, who has sent his good creature sleep from all time by night or by day thus gratifying whom he wills, diffused a portion of it now upon the king.
verses.text_hr: Ali Onaj koji od početka vremena noću i danju šalje dobro stvorenje sna i njime obdaruje koga hoće, upravo ga je tada spustio i na kralja.

verses.text_en: By this sweet and profound influence of the Lord, he was held fast, and thus his unjust purpose was quite frustrated, and his unflinching resolve greatly falsified.
verses.text_hr: Slatka i duboka sila Gospodnja čvrsto ga je obuzela. Tako je njegov nepravedni naum posve osujećen, a njegova nepokolebljiva odluka potpuno izjalovljena.

verses.text_en: But the Jews, having escaped the hour which had been fixed, praised their holy God, and again prayed him who is easily reconciled to display the power of his powerful hand to the arrogant Gentiles.
verses.text_hr: Židovi su, izbjegavši određeni čas, hvalili svojega svetog Boga te ponovno molili Onoga koji se lako smiluje da oholim poganima pokaže snagu svoje moćne ruke.

verses.text_en: The middle of the tenth hour had nearly arrived, when the person who sent invitations, seeing the guests who were invited present, came and shook the king.
verses.text_hr: Već se približila polovica desetoga sata kad je dvorski službenik zadužen za pozive, vidjevši da su pozvani gosti već nazočni, došao i prodrmao kralja.

verses.text_en: He gained his attention with difficulty, and hinting that the mealtime was getting past, talked the matter over with him.
verses.text_hr: Jedva mu je privukao pozornost, a zatim mu dao do znanja da vrijeme objeda prolazi i o tome s njime porazgovarao.

verses.text_en: The king listened to this, and then turning aside to his drinking, commanded the guests to sit down before him.
verses.text_hr: Kralj ga je saslušao, potom se vratio piću i naredio gostima da sjednu pred njim.

verses.text_en: This done, he asked them to enjoy themselves, and to indulge in mirth at this somewhat late hour of the banquet.
verses.text_hr: Kad su sjeli, pozvao ih je da se opuste i predaju veselju u taj već pomalo kasni sat gozbe.

verses.text_en: Conversation grew on, and the king sent for Hermon, and inquired of him, with fierce denunciations, why the Jews had been allowed to outlive that day.
verses.text_hr: Kad se razgovor razvio, kralj je pozvao Hermona i uz žestoke prijetnje upitao ga zašto je Židovima bilo dopušteno da prežive taj dan.

verses.text_en: Hermon explained that he had done his bidding over night; and in this he was confirmed by his friends.
verses.text_hr: Hermon je objasnio da je još tijekom noći učinio što mu je kralj zapovjedio, a njegovi su prijatelji to potvrdili.

verses.text_en: The king, then, with a barbarity exceeding that of Phalaris, said, “They might thank his sleep of that day. Lose no time, and get ready the elephants against tomorrow, as you did before, for the destruction of these accursed Jews.”
verses.text_hr: Tada je kralj, barbarskiji čak i od Falarida, rekao: „Za to mogu zahvaliti mojem današnjem snu. Ne gubi vrijeme, nego za sutra opet pripremi slonove kao i prije, da unište te proklete Židove.“

verses.text_en: When the king said this, the company present were glad, and approved. Then each man went to his own home.
verses.text_hr: Kad je kralj to rekao, nazočno se društvo obradovalo i odobrilo njegove riječi. Potom se svatko vratio svojemu domu.

verses.text_en: They didn’t employ the night in sleep, but in contriving cruel mockeries for those deemed miserable.
verses.text_hr: Noć nisu proveli spavajući, nego smišljajući okrutna izrugivanja onima koje su držali bijednima.

verses.text_en: The morning cock had just crowed, and Hermon, having harnessed the brutes, was stimulating them in the great colonnade.
verses.text_hr: Tek što je zapjevao jutarnji pijetao, Hermon je već upregnuo zvijeri i razdraživao ih u velikoj kolonadi.

verses.text_en: The city crowds were collected together to see the hideous spectacle, and waited impatiently for the dawn.
verses.text_hr: Gradsko se mnoštvo okupilo da vidi jeziv prizor i nestrpljivo je čekalo svitanje.

verses.text_en: The Jews, breathless with momentary suspense, stretched out their hands and prayed the Greatest God, in mournful strains, again to help them speedily.
verses.text_hr: Židovi su, bez daha u neizvjesnosti svakoga trenutka, pružali ruke i u žalobnim molitvama ponovno zaklinjali Svevišnjega Boga da im brzo pomogne.

verses.text_en: The sun’s rays were not yet shining and the king was waiting for his friends when Hermon came to him, calling him out, and saying that his desires could now be realized.
verses.text_hr: Sunčeve zrake još nisu sjale, a kralj je čekao svoje prijatelje, kad mu je Hermon pristupio, pozvao ga van i rekao da se njegove želje sada mogu ostvariti.

verses.text_en: The king, receiving him, was astonished at his unusual invitation. Overwhelmed with a spirit of oblivion about everything, inquired about the object of this earnest preparation.
verses.text_hr: Kad ga je kralj primio, začudio se njegovu neobičnom pozivu. Obuzet duhom zaborava na sve što se dogodilo, upitao je čemu služe te gorljive pripreme.

verses.text_en: But this was the working of that Almighty God who had made him forget all his purpose.
verses.text_hr: To je bilo djelo svemogućega Boga, koji je učinio da kralj zaboravi cijeli svoj naum.

verses.text_en: Hermon and all his friends pointed out the preparation of the animals. They are ready, O king, according to your own strict injunction.
verses.text_hr: Hermon i svi njegovi prijatelji pokazali su mu pripremljene životinje i rekli: „Spremne su, kralju, točno prema tvojoj strogoj zapovijedi.“

verses.text_en: The king was filled with fierce anger at these words, for, by the Providence of God regarding these things, his mind had become entirely confused. He looked hard at Hermon, and threatened him as follows:
verses.text_hr: Na te se riječi kralj razbjesnio jer mu je Božja Providnost u vezi s tim događajima potpuno pomutila um. Oštro je pogledao Hermona i ovako mu zaprijetio:

verses.text_en: “Your parents, or your children, were they here, would have given a large meal to these wild animals, not these innocent Jews, who have loyally served me and my forefathers.
verses.text_hr: „Da su ovdje tvoji roditelji ili djeca, oni bi tim divljim životinjama poslužili kao obilna gozba, a ne ovi nedužni Židovi koji su odano služili meni i mojim precima.

verses.text_en: Had it not been for familiar friendship, and the claims of your office, your life should have gone for theirs.”
verses.text_hr: Da nije našega dugogodišnjeg prijateljstva i dužnosti koju obnašaš, tvoj bi život bio dan umjesto njihovih.“

verses.text_en: Hermon, being threatened in this unexpected and alarming manner, was troubled in his eyes, and his face fell.
verses.text_hr: Hermon se uznemirio zbog te neočekivane i strašne prijetnje; pogled mu se smutio, a lice klonulo.

verses.text_en: The friends, too, stole out one by one, and dismissed the assembled multitudes to their respective occupations.
verses.text_hr: I prijatelji su se jedan po jedan neprimjetno povukli te okupljeno mnoštvo poslali natrag njegovim svakodnevnim poslovima.

verses.text_en: The Jews, having heard of these events, praised the glorious God and King of kings, because they had obtained this help, too, from him.
verses.text_hr: Kad su Židovi čuli što se dogodilo, hvalili su slavnoga Boga i Kralja kraljeva jer su i tu pomoć primili od njega.

verses.text_en: Now the king arranged another banquet in the same way, and proclaimed an invitation to mirth.
verses.text_hr: Kralj je zatim na isti način priredio novu gozbu i objavio poziv na veselje.

verses.text_en: He summoned Hermon to his presence, and said, with threats, “How often, O wretch, must I repeat my orders to you about these same persons?
verses.text_hr: Pozvao je Hermona preda se i uz prijetnje mu rekao: „Koliko ti puta, bijedniče, moram ponavljati svoje zapovijedi o tim istim ljudima?

verses.text_en: Once more, arm the elephants for the extermination of the Jews tomorrow!”
verses.text_hr: Još jednom opremi slonove da sutra istrijebe Židove!“

verses.text_en: His kinsmen, who were reclining with him, wondered at his instability, and thus expressed themselves:
verses.text_hr: Njegovi rođaci, koji su s njim bili za stolom, čudili su se njegovoj nepostojanosti te rekli:

verses.text_en: “O king, how long do you test us, as of men bereft of reason? This is the third time that you have ordered their destruction. When the thing is to be done, you change your mind, and recall your instructions.
verses.text_hr: „Kralju, koliko ćeš nas još iskušavati kao da smo ljudi lišeni razuma? Ovo je već treći put da zapovijedaš njihovo uništenje. A kad treba izvršiti nalog, predomisliš se i opozoveš svoje upute.

verses.text_en: Because of this, the feeling of expectation causes tumult in the city. It swarms with factions, and is continually on the point of being plundered.”
verses.text_hr: Zbog toga iščekivanje izaziva nemir u gradu. Grad vrvi sukobljenim skupinama i neprestano mu prijeti pljačka.“

verses.text_en: The king, just like another Phalaris, a prey to thoughtlessness, made no account of the changes which his own mind had undergone, issuing in the deliverance of the Jews. He swore a fruitless oath, and determined immediately to send them to hades, crushed by the knees and feet of the elephants.
verses.text_hr: Kralj, posve nalik drugom Falaridu i prepušten nepromišljenosti, uopće nije uzimao u obzir promjene vlastita uma koje su dovele do izbavljenja Židova. Zakleo se ispraznom zakletvom i odlučio da ih odmah pošalje u Had, zgnječene koljenima i nogama slonova.

verses.text_en: He would also invade Judea, level its towns with fire and the sword, destroy that temple which the heathen might not enter, and prevent sacrifices ever after being offered up there.
verses.text_hr: Namjeravao je upasti i u Judeju, ognjem i mačem sravniti njezine gradove, razoriti Hram u koji pogani nisu smjeli ulaziti te zauvijek spriječiti prinošenje žrtava na tom mjestu.

verses.text_en: Joyfully his friends broke up, together with his kinsmen; and, trusting in his determination, arranged their forces in guard at the most convenient places of the city.
verses.text_hr: Njegovi prijatelji i rođaci radosno su se razišli. Uzdajući se u njegovu odlučnost, rasporedili su svoje snage kao stražu na najprikladnijim mjestima u gradu.

verses.text_en: The master of the elephants urged the animals into an almost maniacal state, drenched them with incense and wine, and decked them with frightful devices.
verses.text_hr: Nadstojnik slonova dotjerao je životinje gotovo do ludila: obilno ih je napojio vinom i tamjanom te okitio zastrašujućom opremom.

verses.text_en: About early morning, when the city was filled with an immense number of people at the hippodrome, he entered the palace and called the king to the business in hand.
verses.text_hr: U rano jutro, kad se u gradu oko hipodroma okupilo neizmjerno mnoštvo, ušao je u palaču i pozvao kralja da pristupi izvršenju nauma.

verses.text_en: The king’s heart teemed with impious rage; and he rushed forth with the mass, along with the elephants. With unsoftened feelings and pitiless eyes, he longed to gaze at the hard and wretched doom of the previously mentioned Jews.
verses.text_hr: Kraljevo je srce kipjelo od bezbožna bijesa. Izjurio je s mnoštvom i slonovima; neumoljiva srca i nemilosrdna pogleda žudio je promatrati tešku i bijednu sudbinu već spomenutih Židova.

verses.text_en: But the Jews, when the elephants went out at the gate, followed by the armed force. When they saw the dust raised by the throng, and heard the loud cries of the crowd,
verses.text_hr: Kad su Židovi ugledali slonove kako izlaze kroz vrata, praćene naoružanim snagama, te vidjeli prašinu koju je podiglo mnoštvo i čuli glasne povike okupljenih,

verses.text_en: thought that they had come to the last moment of their lives, to the end of what they had tremblingly expected. They gave way, therefore, to lamentations and moans. They kissed each other. Those nearest of kin to each other hung around one another’s necks—fathers hugging their sons and mothers their daughters. Other women held their infants to their breasts, which drew what seemed their last milk.
verses.text_hr: pomislili su da je došao posljednji trenutak njihova života i kraj onoga što su sa strepnjom iščekivali. Prepustili su se naricanju i jecajima. Ljubili su jedni druge, a najbliži rođaci grlili su se oko vrata — očevi sinove, majke kćeri. Druge su žene na prsima držale dojenčad koja je sisala, kako se činilo, posljednje mlijeko.

verses.text_en: Nevertheless, when they reflected upon the help previously granted them from heaven, they prostrated themselves with one accord, removed even the sucking children from the breasts, and
verses.text_hr: Ipak, kad su se prisjetili pomoći koju su već primili s neba, jednodušno su se bacili ničice, odvojili čak i dojenčad od prsa

verses.text_en: sent up an exceedingly great cry asking the Lord of all power to reveal himself, and have mercy upon those who now lay at the gates of hades.
verses.text_hr: te podigli silan vapaj, moleći Gospodara svake sile da se objavi i smiluje onima koji sada leže na vratima Hada.

verses.text_en: Then Eleazar, an illustrious priest of the country, who had attained to length of days, and whose life had been adorned with virtue, caused the elders who were around him to cease to cry out to the holy God, and prayed this:
verses.text_hr: Tada je Eleazar, ugledni domaći svećenik koji je doživio duboku starost i svoj život ukrasio krepošću, pozvao starješine oko sebe da prestanu vapiti svetomu Bogu pa se ovako pomolio:

verses.text_en: “O king, mighty in power, most high, Almighty God, who regulates the whole creation with your tender mercy,
verses.text_hr: „Kralju silne moći, Svevišnji, svemogući Bože, koji svojim nježnim milosrđem upravljaš svim stvorenjem,

verses.text_en: look at the seed of Abraham, at the children of the sanctified Jacob, your sanctified inheritance, O Father, now being wrongfully destroyed as foreigners in a foreign land.
verses.text_hr: pogledaj Abrahamovo potomstvo, djecu posvećenoga Jakova, svoju posvećenu baštinu, Oče, koju sada nepravedno uništavaju kao tuđince u tuđoj zemlji.

verses.text_en: You destroyed Pharaoh with his army of chariots when that lord of this same Egypt was uplifted with lawless daring and loud-sounding tongue. Shedding the beams of your mercy upon the race of Israel, you overwhelmed him and his proud army.
verses.text_hr: Faraona si s njegovom vojskom bojnih kola uništio kad se taj vladar upravo ovoga Egipta uzoholio u bezakonoj drskosti i razmetljivu govoru. Svojim si milosrđem obasjao izraelski rod, a njega i njegovu oholu vojsku potopio.

verses.text_en: When Sennacherim, the grievous king of the Assyrians, exulting in his countless army, had subdued the whole land with his spear and was lifting himself against your holy city with boastings grievous to be endured, you, O Lord, demolished him and displayed your might to many nations.
verses.text_hr: Kad se Sanherib, okrutni kralj Asiraca, uzdao u svoju bezbrojnu vojsku, kopljem pokorio svu zemlju i uzdizao se protiv tvojega svetoga grada nepodnošljivim hvalisanjem, ti si ga, Gospodine, satro i svoju moć pokazao mnogim narodima.

verses.text_en: When the three friends in the land of Babylon of their own will exposed their lives to the fire rather than serve vain things, you sent a moist coolness through the fiery furnace, and brought the fire on all their adversaries.
verses.text_hr: Kad su tri prijatelja u zemlji Babilonu svojevoljno izložila živote ognju radije nego da služe ispraznim stvarima, ti si kroz užarenu peć poslao rosnu svježinu, a oganj okrenuo na sve njihove protivnike.

verses.text_en: It was you who, when Daniel was hurled, through slander and envy, as a prey to lions down below, brought him back again unharmed to light.
verses.text_hr: Ti si Daniela, kojega su zbog klevete i zavisti bacili u dubinu kao plijen lavovima, ponovno izveo neozlijeđena na svjetlo.

verses.text_en: When Jonah was pining away in the belly of the sea-born monster, you looked at him, O Father, and recovered him to the sight of his own.
verses.text_hr: Kad je Jona kopnio u utrobi morske nemani, pogledao si na njega, Oče, i vratio ga da ga njegovi ponovno ugledaju.

verses.text_en: Now, you who hate insolence, you who abound in mercy, you who are the protector of all things, appear quickly to those of the race of Israel, who are insulted by abhorred, lawless gentiles.
verses.text_hr: Sada ti, koji mrziš oholost, obiluješ milosrđem i štitiš sve, brzo se objavi pripadnicima izraelskoga roda koje vrijeđaju odvratni bezakoni pogani.

verses.text_en: If our life during our exile has been stained with iniquity, deliver us from the hand of the enemy, and destroy us, O Lord, by the death which you prefer.
verses.text_hr: Ako se naš život u izgnanstvu okaljao bezakonjem, izbavi nas iz ruke neprijatelja, a zatim nas ti, Gospodine, usmrti smrću koju sam izabereš.

verses.text_en: Don’t let the vain-minded congratulate vain idols at the destruction of your beloved, saying, ‘Their god didn’t deliver them.’
verses.text_hr: Ne dopusti da se isprazni umovi zbog propasti tvojih ljubljenih čestitaju ispraznim idolima i govore: ‘Njihov ih bog nije izbavio.’

verses.text_en: You who are All-powerful and Almighty, O Eternal One, behold! Have mercy on us who are being withdrawn from life, like traitors, by the unreasoning insolence of lawless men.
verses.text_hr: Ti koji si svesilan i svemoguć, Vječni, pogledaj nas! Smiluj se nama koje bezumna drskost bezakonika odvlači iz života kao izdajice.

verses.text_en: Let the heathen cower before your invincible might today, O glorious One, who have all power to save the race of Jacob.
verses.text_hr: Neka se pogani danas prestraše pred tvojom nepobjedivom silom, Slavni, koji imaš svu moć spasiti Jakovljev rod.

verses.text_en: The whole band of infants and their parents ask you with tears.
verses.text_hr: Čitavo mnoštvo dojenčadi i njihovih roditelja sa suzama te moli.

verses.text_en: Let it be shown to all the nations that you are with us, O Lord, and have not turned your face away from us, but as you said that you would not forget them even in the land of their enemies, so fulfill this saying, O Lord.”
verses.text_hr: Pokaži svim narodima da si s nama, Gospodine, i da nisi odvratio svoje lice od nas. Kao što si rekao da nas nećeš zaboraviti čak ni u zemlji naših neprijatelja, tako ispuni tu riječ, Gospodine.“

verses.text_en: Now, at the time that Eleazar had ended his prayer, the king came along to the hippodrome with the wild animals, and with his tumultuous power.
verses.text_hr: Kad je Eleazar završio molitvu, kralj je s divljim životinjama i svojom bučnom vojnom silom stigao do hipodroma.

verses.text_en: When the Jews saw this, they uttered a loud cry to heaven so that the adjacent valleys resounded and caused an irrepressible lamentation throughout the army.
verses.text_hr: Kad su to Židovi vidjeli, podigli su prema nebu tako glasan vapaj da su odjeknule obližnje doline, a cijelom se vojskom proširilo nezaustavljivo naricanje.

verses.text_en: Then the all-glorious, all-powerful, and true God, displayed his holy countenance, and opened the gates of heaven, from which two angels, dreadful of form, came down and were visible to all but the Jews.
verses.text_hr: Tada je sveslavni, svemoćni i istiniti Bog pokazao svoje sveto lice i otvorio nebeska vrata. Iz njih su sišla dva anđela strašna izgleda, vidljiva svima osim Židovima.

verses.text_en: They stood opposite, and filled the enemies’ army with confusion and cowardice, and bound them with immoveable shackles.
verses.text_hr: Stali su nasuprot neprijateljima, ispunili njihovu vojsku smetenošću i kukavičlukom te ih sputali nepomičnim okovima.

verses.text_en: A cold shudder came over the person of the king, and oblivion paralyzed the vehemence of his spirit.
verses.text_hr: Kraljevim je tijelom prostrujio hladan drhtaj, a zaborav je ukočio žestinu njegova duha.

verses.text_en: They turned back the animals on the armed forces who followed them; and the animals trampled them and destroyed them.
verses.text_hr: Anđeli su životinje okrenuli protiv naoružanih snaga koje su ih slijedile, a one su ih pogazile i uništile.

verses.text_en: The king’s wrath was converted into compassion; and he wept at the things he had devised.
verses.text_hr: Kraljev se gnjev pretvorio u samilost te je zaplakao zbog svega što je bio smislio.

verses.text_en: For when he heard the cry, and saw them all on the verge of destruction, with tears he angrily threatened his friends, saying,
verses.text_hr: Kad je čuo vapaj i vidio da se svi nalaze pred uništenjem, u suzama je ljutito zaprijetio svojim prijateljima govoreći:

verses.text_en: “You have governed badly, and have exceeded tyrants in cruelty. You have labored to deprive me, your benefactor, at once of my dominion and my life, by secretly devising measures injurious to the kingdom.
verses.text_hr: „Loše ste upravljali i okrutnošću nadmašili tirane. Potajno smišljajući mjere pogubne za kraljevstvo nastojali ste mene, svojega dobročinitelja, istodobno lišiti vlasti i života.

verses.text_en: Who has gathered here, unreasonably removing each from his home, those who, in fidelity to us, had held the fortresses of the country?
verses.text_hr: Tko je nerazumno odveo iz doma i ovdje okupio one koji su nam vjerno čuvali tvrđave zemlje?

verses.text_en: Who has consigned to unmerited punishments those who in good will toward us from the beginning have in all things surpassed all nations, and who often have engaged in the most dangerous undertakings?
verses.text_hr: Tko je nezasluženim kaznama predao ljude koji su nam od početka iskazivali toliku odanost da su u svemu nadmašili sve narode i mnogo se puta upuštali u najopasnije pothvate?

verses.text_en: Loose, loose the unjust bonds! Send them to their homes in peace, begging pardon for what has been done.
verses.text_hr: Oslobodite ih, oslobodite nepravednih okova! Pošaljite ih u miru njihovim domovima i molite ih da oproste ono što im je učinjeno.

verses.text_en: Release the sons of the almighty living God of heaven, who from our ancestors’ times until now has granted a glorious and uninterrupted prosperity to our affairs.”
verses.text_hr: Pustite sinove svemogućega, živog Boga nebeskoga, koji je od vremena naših predaka sve do danas našim poslovima davao slavan i neprekinut napredak.“

verses.text_en: He said these things, and they, released the same moment, having now escaped death, praised God their holy Savior.
verses.text_hr: Tako je rekao, a oni su istoga trenutka oslobođeni. Izbjegavši smrt, hvalili su Boga, svojega svetog Spasitelja.

verses.text_en: The king then departed to the city, and called his financier to himself, and asked him provide a seven days’ quantity of wine and other materials for feasting for the Jews. He decided that they should keep a cheerful festival of deliverance in the very place in which they expected to meet with their destruction.
verses.text_hr: Kralj se zatim vratio u grad, pozvao upravitelja financija i naložio mu da Židovima osigura vina i druge hrane za sedam dana gozbe. Odlučio je da upravo na mjestu na kojem su očekivali propast radosno proslave blagdan izbavljenja.

verses.text_en: Then they who were before despised and near to hades, yes, rather advanced into it, partook of the cup of salvation, instead of a grievous and lamentable death. Full of exultation, they apportioned the place intended for their fall and burial into banqueting booths.
verses.text_hr: Tako su oni koji su prije bili prezreni i blizu Hada — štoviše, već gotovo zakoračili u nj — primili čašu spasenja umjesto teške i žalosne smrti. Ispunjeni klicanjem, prostor namijenjen njihovu padu i grobu podijelili su na sjenice za gozbu.

verses.text_en: Ceasing their miserable strain of woe, they took up the subject of their fatherland, singing in praise to God their wonder-working Savior. All groans and all wailing were laid aside. They formed dances as a sign of peaceful joy.
verses.text_hr: Prestali su sa žalosnim naricanjem i zapjevali o svojoj domovini, hvaleći Boga, čudotvornoga Spasitelja. Odbacili su svaki jecaj i svaki plač te zaplesali u znak mirne radosti.

verses.text_en: So the king also collected a number of guests for the occasion, and returned unceasing thanks with much magnificence for the unexpected deliverance afforded him.
verses.text_hr: I kralj je za tu prigodu okupio mnoštvo gostiju te uz veliku raskoš bez prestanka zahvaljivao za neočekivano izbavljenje koje mu je bilo darovano.

verses.text_en: Those who had marked them out as for death and for carrion, and had registered them with joy, howled aloud, and were clothed with shame, and had the fire of their rage ingloriously put out.
verses.text_hr: Oni koji su ih označili za smrt i strvinu te ih s veseljem popisivali sada su glasno zavijali, zaodjenuti sramotom, dok se plamen njihova bijesa neslavno ugasio.

verses.text_en: But the Jews, as we just said, instituted a dance, and then gave themselves up to feasting, glad thanksgiving, and psalms.
verses.text_hr: Židovi su pak, kao što smo upravo rekli, priredili ples, a potom se predali gozbi, radosnom zahvaljivanju i psalmima.

verses.text_en: They made a public ordinance to commemorate these things for generations to come, as long as they should be sojourners. They thus established these days as days of mirth, not for the purpose of drinking or luxury, but because God had saved them.
verses.text_hr: Donijeli su javnu uredbu da se ti događaji spominju u budućim naraštajima dokle god budu živjeli kao došljaci. Te su dane ustanovili kao dane radosti, ne radi opijanja ili raskoši, nego zato što ih je Bog spasio.

verses.text_en: They requested the king to send them back to their homes.
verses.text_hr: Zamolili su kralja da ih pošalje natrag njihovim domovima.

verses.text_en: They were being enrolled from the twenty-fifth of Pachon to the fourth of Epiphi, a period of forty days. The measures taken for their destruction lasted from the fifth of Epiphi till the seventh, that is, three days.
verses.text_hr: Popisivali su ih od dvadeset petoga dana mjeseca Pahona do četvrtoga dana Epifija, dakle četrdeset dana. Mjere za njihovo uništenje trajale su od petoga do sedmoga dana Epifija, to jest tri dana.

verses.text_en: The Ruler over all during this time manifested his mercy gloriously, and delivered them all together unharmed.
verses.text_hr: Vladar svega tijekom toga je vremena slavno očitovao svoje milosrđe i sve ih zajedno izbavio neozlijeđene.

verses.text_en: They feasted upon the king’s provision up to the fourteenth day, then asked to be sent away.
verses.text_hr: Gostili su se kraljevim zalihama sve do četrnaestoga dana, a zatim zatražili da ih pošalje kući.

verses.text_en: The king commended them, and wrote the following letter, of magnanimous import for them, to the commanders of every city:
verses.text_hr: Kralj ih je pohvalio i zapovjednicima svakoga grada napisao sljedeće pismo, koje je prema njima bilo puno velikodušnosti:

verses.text_en: “King Ptolemy Philopator to the commanders throughout Egypt, and to all who are set over affairs, joy and strength.
verses.text_hr: „Kralj Ptolemej Filopator zapovjednicima po cijelom Egiptu i svima postavljenima nad državnim poslovima: radost i snaga!

verses.text_en: We, too, and our children are well. God has directed our affairs as we wish.
verses.text_hr: I mi i naša djeca dobro smo. Bog je naše poslove usmjerio prema našim željama.

verses.text_en: Certain of our friends out of malice vehemently urged us to punish the Jews of our realm in a body, with the infliction of a monstrous punishment.
verses.text_hr: Neki su nas naši prijatelji iz zlobe žestoko nagovarali da sve Židove u našem kraljevstvu zajednički kaznimo stravičnom kaznom.

verses.text_en: They pretended that our affairs would never be in a good state till this took place. Such, they said, was the hatred borne by the Jews to all other people.
verses.text_hr: Tvrdili su da naši poslovi neće nikada biti u dobrom stanju dok se to ne izvrši, jer Židovi, navodno, toliko mrze sve druge ljude.

verses.text_en: They brought them fettered in grievous chains as slaves, no, as traitors. Without enquiry or examination they endeavored to annihilate them. They buckled themselves with a savage cruelty, worse than Scythian custom.
verses.text_hr: Doveli su ih okovane teškim lancima kao robove — štoviše, kao izdajice. Bez istrage i provjere pokušali su ih istrijebiti, opasavši se divljačkom okrutnošću gorom i od skitskih običaja.

verses.text_en: For this cause we severely threatened them; yet, with the clemency which we usually extend to all men, we at length permitted them to live. Finding that the God of heaven cast a shield of protection over the Jews so as to preserve them, and that he fought for them as a father always fights for his sons,
verses.text_hr: Zbog toga smo im strogo zaprijetili. Ipak smo, iz blagosti koju običavamo iskazivati svim ljudima, naposljetku dopustili Židovima da žive. Uvidjeli smo da ih nebeski Bog štiti poput štita i čuva te se za njih bori kao što se otac uvijek bori za svoje sinove.

verses.text_en: and taking into consideration their constancy and fidelity toward us and toward our ancestors, we have, as we ought, acquitted them of every sort of charge.
verses.text_hr: Uzevši u obzir i njihovu postojanost i vjernost prema nama i našim precima, oslobodili smo ih, kako je i pravedno, svake optužbe.

verses.text_en: We have dismissed them to their several homes, telling all men everywhere to do them no wrong, or unrighteously revile them about the past.
verses.text_hr: Otpustili smo ih svakoga njegovu domu i svima posvuda zapovjedili da im ne nanose zlo niti ih nepravedno vrijeđaju zbog onoga što se dogodilo.

verses.text_en: For know this, that should we conceive any evil design, or in any way aggrieve them, we shall ever have as our adversary, not man, but the highest God, the ruler of all might. From Him there will be no escape, as the avenger of such deeds. Farewell.”
verses.text_hr: Znajte: smislimo li protiv njih ikakvo zlo ili ih na bilo koji način ožalostimo, za protivnika nećemo imati čovjeka, nego Svevišnjega Boga, Vladara sve sile. Od njega, osvetnika takvih djela, neće biti bijega. Budite zdravo!“

verses.text_en: When they had received this letter, they didn’t hurry to depart immediately. They petitioned the king to be allowed to inflict fitting punishment upon those of their race who had willingly transgressed the holy god, and the law of God.
verses.text_hr: Kad su primili to pismo, nisu odmah požurili na put. Zamolili su kralja da im dopusti primjereno kazniti pripadnike njihova roda koji su svojevoljno prestupili protiv svetoga Boga i Božjega Zakona.

verses.text_en: They alleged that men who had for their bellies’ sake transgressed the ordinances of God, would never be faithful to the interests of the king.
verses.text_hr: Tvrdili su da oni koji su radi svojega trbuha pogazili Božje odredbe nikada neće biti vjerni ni kraljevim interesima.

verses.text_en: The king admitted the truth of this reasoning, and commended them. Full power was given them, without warrant or special commission, to destroy those who had transgressed the law of God boldly in every part of the king’s dominions.
verses.text_hr: Kralj je priznao istinitost tih riječi i pohvalio ih. Dao im je punu vlast da, bez pojedinačnoga naloga ili posebne ovlasti, po svim dijelovima kraljevstva pogube one koji su se drsko ogriješili o Božji Zakon.

verses.text_en: Their priests, then, as it was appropriate, saluted him with good wishes, and all the people echoed with the “Hallelujah!” Then they joyfully departed.
verses.text_hr: Njihovi su mu svećenici potom, kako je dolikovalo, uputili dobre želje, a sav je narod odgovorio: „Aleluja!“ Zatim su radosno otišli.

verses.text_en: Then they punished and shamefully destroyed every polluted Jew that fell in their way,
verses.text_hr: Kažnjavali su i na sramotan način pogubljivali svakoga oskvrnjenog Židova na kojega su naišli.

verses.text_en: slaying this way, in that day, more than three hundred men, and esteeming this destruction of the wicked a season of joy.
verses.text_hr: Tako su toga dana ubili više od tri stotine ljudi, a uništenje zlikovaca smatrali su vremenom radosti.

verses.text_en: They themselves having held closely to their God to death, and having enjoyed a full deliverance, departed from the city garlanded with sweet-flowered wreaths of every kind. Uttering exclamations of joy, with songs of praise, and melodious hymns, they thanked the God of their fathers, the eternal Savior of Israel.
verses.text_hr: Oni sami ostali su čvrsto uz svojega Boga sve do smrti i primili potpuno izbavljenje. Izišli su iz grada ovjenčani vijencima svakovrsna mirisnog cvijeća; uz radosne povike, pjesme hvale i skladne hvalospjeve zahvaljivali su Bogu svojih otaca, vječnom Spasitelju Izraela.

verses.text_en: Having arrived at Ptolemais, called from the specialty of that district “Rose-bearing”, where the fleet, in accordance with the general wish, waited for them seven days,
verses.text_hr: Stigli su u Ptolemaidu, koju su zbog osobitosti toga kraja zvali „Ružonosna“. Ondje ih je, prema zajedničkoj želji, brodovlje čekalo sedam dana.

verses.text_en: they partook of a banquet of deliverance, for the king generously granted them all the means of securing a return home.
verses.text_hr: Sudjelovali su u gozbi izbavljenja jer im je kralj velikodušno dao sve što im je bilo potrebno za povratak kući.

verses.text_en: They were accordingly brought back in peace, while they gave utterance to appropriate thanks; and they determined to observe these days during their sojourn as days of joyfulness.
verses.text_hr: Tako su u miru vraćeni svojim domovima, iskazujući primjerenu zahvalnost, i odlučili su da će tijekom svojega boravka u tuđini te dane svetkovati kao dane radosti.

verses.text_en: These they registered as sacred upon a pillar, when they had dedicated the place of their festivity to be one of prayer. They departed unharmed, free, abundant in joy, preserved by the king’s command, by land, by sea, and by river, each to his own home.
verses.text_hr: Upisali su ih kao svete dane na stupu, pošto su mjesto svoje svečanosti posvetili za molitvu. Otišli su neozlijeđeni, slobodni i ispunjeni radošću; kraljeva ih je zapovijed štitila na kopnu, moru i rijeci dok se svaki nije vratio svojemu domu.

verses.text_en: They had more weight than before among their enemies, and were honored and feared. No one in any way robbed them of their goods.
verses.text_hr: Među svojim su neprijateljima sada imali veći ugled nego prije; bili su čašćeni i ulijevali strah. Nitko im ni na koji način nije oduzeo imovinu.

verses.text_en: Every man received back his own, according to inventory, those who had obtained their goods, giving them up with the greatest terror. For the greatest God made perfect wonders for their salvation.
verses.text_hr: Svatko je prema popisu ponovno primio ono što mu je pripadalo, a oni koji su uzeli njihova dobra vraćali su ih u najvećem strahu. Jer je Svevišnji Bog za njihovo spasenje učinio savršena čudesa.

verses.text_en: Blessed be the Redeemer of Israel forever! Amen.
verses.text_hr: Blagoslovljen bio Otkupitelj Izraela zauvijek! Amen.
